claims.text: Bias and unfairness issues in information retrieval systems can be unified as distribution mismatch problems.
Neural retrieval models favor LLM-generated content over human-authored content with similar semantics.
LLM-based IR models tend to give preference to candidate documents or items from specific input positions.
LLM-based IR models prioritize candidate items popular within the LLM pre-training corpora in addition to the fine-tuning datasets.
LLM-based evaluators exhibit selection bias by favoring responses at specific positions or with specific option tokens.
LLM-based evaluators demonstrate egocentric bias by preferring outputs generated by themselves or models from the same family.
Mitigation strategies for bias and unfairness in LLM-integrated IR systems can be categorized into data sampling and distribution reconstruction.

evidence.description: The paper formulates both bias and unfairness as distribution mismatch problems where predicted distribution P(R_hat) differs from ground truth distribution P(R).
Recent studies highlight that modern retrieval models, especially those leveraging neural matching techniques, tend to favor LLM-generated content over human-authored content with similar semantics.
LLM-based models often show a preference for content positioned at the beginning or end of a list, exhibiting a 'lost in the middle' phenomenon.

Unlike conventional models, LLM-based IR models do not merely reflect the popularity distributions of the target finetuning dataset; they are also inclined to retrieve or recommend items popular in the pre-training corpora.
gpt-3.5-turbo exhibits a preference for choice 'C', while llama-30B shows a preference for choice 'A' across various multiple-choice evaluation benchmarks.
When acting as evaluators, LLMs demonstrate a clear bias towards outputs generated by themselves over those from other models or human contributors.
Mitigation strategies are systematically structured into data sampling (data augmentation, data filtering) and distribution reconstruction (rebalancing, regularization, prompting).

methodologies.name: Structured Literature Review and Theoretical Taxonomy
methodologies.description: A comprehensive survey systematically organizing literature on bias and unfairness across three IR lifecycle stages and mapping mitigation strategies to a unified distribution alignment framework.
conditions: LLM integration into Information Retrieval lifecycle
Data Collection, Model Development, and Result Evaluation stages

limitations.text: Current research on bias and unfairness at the intersection of LLMs and IR is predominantly empirical and lacks robust theoretical analysis and guarantees.
Existing mitigation strategies primarily address individual instances of bias or unfairness in isolation rather than through a unified framework.
Most current evaluation benchmarks rely on simulated environments rather than large-scale, real-world, and dynamic datasets.

future_work.text: Exploring novel strategies to interrupt feedback loops between users, models, and information that reinforce biases and unfairness over time.
Developing unified mitigation frameworks capable of addressing multiple non-isolated types of bias and unfairness simultaneously.
Establishing rigorous analytical frameworks to provide theoretical analysis and guarantees for debiasing and fairness methods in LLM-IR systems.
Collecting large-scale real-world datasets and developing dynamic benchmarks alongside systematic evaluation protocols for bias and unfairness.
